sections.h2: What does the Lyon County Assessor do?
sections.html:
The Lyon County Assessor's Office sets the market value and classification of each parcel as of January 2 each year. It is at 607 West Main Street, Marshall, MN 56258.

Minnesota statutes require the assessor to inspect every property at least once in a five-year interval, and the county describes a quintile review that relies on a physical, in-person inspection to gather property characteristics. Valuation notices go out each spring, and local, county and state boards of equalization meet every year as a forum to appeal value or classification. The office also runs the Green Acres, blind or disabled homestead and local option disaster abatement programs, and takes homestead applications.

sections.h2: What does the Lyon County Auditor/Treasurer handle?
sections.html:
The Auditor/Treasurer is the county's chief financial officer and its property tax administrator, and also its chief election official. For taxes, that means calculating each bill, collecting current and delinquent real estate tax, managing escrow, settling receipts with the taxing entities, running forfeited land proceedings and handling special assessments including ditches.

By statute the Auditor/Treasurer is also a member of the County Board of Equalization. The county's online tools let you find and pay your property tax online and search property records, valuation, classification and sales information. If your parcel has ditch assessments, ask this office to itemize them.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Lyon County for a seller?
sections.html:
Lyon County has Marshall as its seat and makes up the Marshall Micropolitan Statistical Area. It covers 715 square miles of land, second only to Itasca among the four counties in this series.

The Yellow Medicine, Redwood and Cottonwood rivers cross the county on their way northeast, and the land is low rolling hills. The state legislature established the county in 1868 and 1869, naming it for Army officer Nathaniel Lyon, who was killed in the Civil War in 1861. In 1873 the western 43% became Lincoln County. Cities are Balaton, Cottonwood, Florence, Garvin, Ghent, Lynd, Marshall, Minneota, Russell, Taunton and Tracy.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 25,684 people, only 0.6% above 2020. Lyon is the most renter-heavy of the four counties: the owner-occupied rate is 72.5% for 2020 to 2024, and the 2020 census counted 33.6% of occupied units as renter-occupied.

  • Housing units in July 2025: 11,437, with just 23 building permits in 2025.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $200,700, the lowest of the four.
  • Median gross rent: $781; median household income: $75,303.
  • Mean commute: 14.6 minutes, the shortest of the four.

sections.h2: What do the 2020 census and QuickFacts say about Lyon County homes and jobs?
sections.html:
Lyon County is more urban than the other three counties here: 53.5% of residents lived in urban areas in 2020, and the median age was 37.5. The county had 10,137 households in 11,180 housing units, with 9.3% vacant and a rental vacancy rate of 12.5%.

Census QuickFacts lists 12,732 people employed at employer establishments in 2023 across 814 establishments, and 2022 retail sales of $650.65 million, or $25,583 per resident, the highest per-person figure of the four counties. Bachelor's degree attainment is 31.1%, foreign-born residents make up 6.1%, and 11.2% of people age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home.

  • Two airports serve the county: Southwest Minnesota Regional Airport (MML) and Tracy Municipal Airport (TKC).
  • Camden State Park and Garvin State Park are inside the county, along with several state wildlife management areas.
  • The median home value of $200,700 is lower than in Isanti ($306,200) or Le Sueur ($316,500), and median gross rent is $781 a month.

sections.h2: When are Lyon County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Minnesota sets the schedule for Lyon County like every other county: half before May 16 and half before October 16 when a bill is over $100. Smaller bills are paid once, at the first-half date.

Lyon County tax dates and penalty rules from Minnesota law
ItemRule
First halfBefore May 16
Second halfBefore October 16
Qualifying seasonal commercial propertyFirst half before June 1, with an affidavit
Agricultural second halfNo penalty if paid by November 15
Late penalty cap8% homestead, 12% nonhomestead

Source: Minnesota Statutes section 279.01. A homestead owner in the National Guard or a reserve component on federal active service gets a four-month grace period with no penalty, and must send a copy of orders or form DD214 with the payment.

sections.h2: How do homestead applications work in Lyon County?
sections.html:
Fill out the homestead application online and print it, or print a blank and fill it out by hand. Return it by mail to the Lyon County Assessor's Office, 607 West Main Street, Marshall, MN 56258, or put it in the drop box at the rear entrance of the Lyon County Government Center.

One local exception: if the property is inside the City of Marshall, call 507-537-6771 to file for homestead. The county says homestead is the program it is asked about most often, and it has a plain-language FAQ on what a homestead is and why it matters. Classification matters most when a payment is late, because the penalty on a nonhomestead parcel starts at 4% instead of 2%.

The state's Homestead Credit Refund is a separate benefit from the Department of Revenue. Its due date is August 15 and it can be filed for up to one year after that date.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Lyon County valuation?
sections.html:
Read the spring notice, call the assessor with your evidence, and then use the local, county or state board of equalization meetings the office describes if you still disagree. The Assessor's FAQ page lists each step, including what evidence to bring to the board.

If you take the matter to court, Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 says a petition must be served on the county auditor and filed with the district court administrator by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. A Tax Court appeal can begin after the valuation notice arrives and has to begin before May 1. The statute also gives an owner 60 days from the notice mailing date when a change in value or class is not announced until after February 28.

sections.h2: What should a Lyon County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the Auditor/Treasurer for the amount owed on your parcel, including penalty and any ditch or other special assessment, and compare it with your closing date. Ask the Assessor whether the homestead classification still matches how the house is used.

The Assessor's online property search shows the property record card, valuation, classification and characteristics for a parcel, and a separate tax information page shows statements and sales. Print the record card before you list, so the numbers you quote match the county's.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a Lyon County homestead application?
faqs.a: Lyon County Assessor's Office, 607 West Main Street, Marshall, MN 56258. There is also a drop box at the rear entrance of the Lyon County Government Center.

faqs.q: Who do I call to file homestead for a house inside Marshall?
faqs.a: Call 507-537-6771. The county says properties within the City of Marshall file through that number.

faqs.q: How often does the Lyon County assessor inspect a property?
faqs.a: At least once in a five-year interval, under Minnesota law. The county uses a quintile review that includes an on-site, in-person inspection.

faqs.q: What is the court deadline to challenge a Lyon County tax?
faqs.a: April 30 of the year the tax is payable for a district court petition. A Tax Court appeal must start before May 1, under Minnesota Statutes section 278.01.

faqs.q: What is the largest late penalty on a Lyon County rental?
faqs.a: 12% of the unpaid tax, which is the cap for nonhomestead property under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01. Homestead property is capped at 8%.
